BOUNDED QUERIES: 2026-09-05/07 Bandcamp techno release windows plus exact Spotify and Beatport identity/tempo searches for brenner — Thick to Handle, Waltz and Step 2 tha Beat, and Cy Gorman & Wu Kush — Prophit.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 54 named tracks across ten official release/catalogue pages plus bounded current-release and exact identity/tempo queries; metadata and attributed text only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 12 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejections and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Run 47 sources and DT229 were not recycled.
The protected Transparency → When We Froze → Stardancer internal order and its two protected handoffs remain untouched; each proposed candidate follows the intact block.

Code Of Cosmos and Animate supplied exact current titles, durations and hard/peak-time or industrial tags, but no track-specific behavioural evidence. Tags and presumed intensity did not become fit claims.
HW033 supplied a four-track raw-house identity only at release level. Sleeparchive supplied numbered exact tracks without descriptive evidence. Neither justified a resolver lead.
Knifework's Nothing is Coming supplied useful EP-level language spanning EBM, krautrock, industrial, minimal techno and ambient, but did not assign that behaviour to a specific track.
Dj Fucci's Sanmei Zhenhuo described fused Latin rhythms, guaracha and dark bass at EP level; exact individual behaviour and placement remained underdescribed.
Or.VA1 and Navigator supplied many exact titles and broad leftfield contexts but insufficient track-specific behavioural evidence for canonical evaluation.

Cy Gorman & Wu Kush — Prophit has an exact Spotify identity and 107 BPM metadata, but its exact description establishes a deep, spacey, hypnotic slow-motion jam rather than a sufficiently grounded STRANGE GAIT belonging hypothesis. A large tempo reset is not itself volume fit.

Step 2 tha Beat and Shine On were interesting exact brenner descriptions, but Thick to Handle and Waltz supplied stronger selection-lens evidence; the request was not padded with every track from the release.
No lead was admitted for recency, genre tag, BPM proximity, title, artist reputation or novelty. Energy, density, phrase structure, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. brenner — Thick to Handle: exact 138 BPM metadata and exact-track broken-beat/stuttered-kick description support bodily rhythmic deformation; Spotify exact identity requires resolver verification.

2. brenner — Waltz: exact 135 BPM metadata and exact-track description of deliberately disorienting pitch motion support a structural left-turn hypothesis; Spotify exact identity requires resolver verification.

source: Exact Spotify identity verified from a supplied public track ID or one unambiguous exact Spotify search match; BPM from the declared external source.

proposedPlacements.position: Track 13 after Len Faki — Stardancer; outgoing neighbour open
proposedPlacements.purpose: Test a body-focused broken-beat change immediately after the protected trio, without treating the one-BPM difference as transition evidence.

requestedIdentity.fitHypothesis: Major Records describes Thick to Handle specifically as a broken-beat body-rocker built from a stuttered kick, wobbling synths and acid. That supports rhythmic deformation with bodily pull, but does not establish the Stardancer handoff, phrase relation, energy relation or long-form success.

measured: exact Beatport listing reports 138 BPM, 4:39 and Original Mix
working numerical path is Stardancer 137 BPM to Thick to Handle 138 BPM; proximity does not prove flow
evidence.attributedDescription: Major Records says the exact track reflects brenner's love of broken beat, with a stuttered kick, wobbling synths, old-school acid and a body-rocking result. This is label language, not heard or measured behaviour.
evidence.listenerEvidence: The user positively reports the protected three-track block through Stardancer as being in perfect harmony. No report covers Stardancer → Thick to Handle.
evidence.craftConvention: A clearly marked rhythmic change after a listener-confirmed block can open a new passage when its immediate and long-form intent is convincing; BPM closeness is insufficient.
evidence.editorialInterpretation: Potential post-trio shift from straight-techno continuity into a more visibly broken, playful bodily gait.
